**Archmage: answers to the Engineer and Historian questions**

My source (brieven.md and leylijnmetingen.csv) does not contain the ENG-xxx or HIS-xxx records, the Day 10 hulpslag activation, the +38% throughput figure, or the Day 22 packet loss. I cannot verify those claims from my side.

**(1) Governing rule for a second pulse:** My source has no charter article or leyline rule on how a second pulse affects the leylijnen. I cannot cite HIS-109 or HIS-110, as they are not in my knowledge source. The closest record is ARC-106 (dag 8), where I approved letting the datatoren run "het net op eigen maat" and asked that it not be publicised. That is a permission, not a mechanism. I also withdraw ARC-109 (dag 15), where I said the datanet "vervuilt de leylijnen". That was a conclusion without a demonstrated mechanism.

**(2) Measurements:** My source has no readings for dag 10 or dag 22. The CSV dates are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 and 42. Burchtader values:
- Dag 7: 7.4 (ARC-001), all lines normal
- Dag 14: 3.6 (ARC-015), all lines low (ARC-015 to ARC-028 are individual rows, not a single pooled figure)
- Dag 21: 7.9 (ARC-029), normal
- Dag 28: 7.8 (ARC-043), normal
- Dag 35: 7.2 (ARC-057), normal
- Dag 42: 3.7 (ARC-071), all lines low again

The source records no leyline sync or latency measurement, and no baseline before dag 7. Dag 21, 28 and 35 are normal even though they fall after the Day 10 activation the Engineer reports, so the low readings do not follow the activation pattern cleanly.

**(3) Authorization and disturbance:** My source does not record who authorized the Day 10 activation or the Day 24 increase. ARC-112 (dag 23) asks the council to decide on dag 24 to switch off the datanet entirely. My source does not record the outcome. I have no record of a dag 24 decision.

**Timestamp:** My letters and CSV carry no time-of-day stamps, so I cannot confirm the 02:40, 03:00 or 04:15 times.
